summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of recurrent venous thromboembolism, IVC filter, chronic hemoptysis, COPD, and chronic pain was admitted for chest pain and hemoptysis. Imaging revealed new bilateral pulmonary emboli in the segmental and subsegmental branches of both lower lobes, with no evidence of right heart strain. He was treated with heparin initially, then transitioned to adjusted-dose enoxaparin (100 mg BID) due to recent weight loss. An ultrasound showed a superficial basilic vein thrombus in the left arm but no DVT in the legs. Pain was managed with limited oxycodone due to substance use concerns, and anxiety was addressed with hydroxyzine. The simvastatin dose was reduced to 20 mg daily due to interaction risk with amlodipine. He stabilized, remained asymptomatic, and was discharged home with close follow-up and strict adherence instructions for anticoagulation.
